correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier autocorrelation identity and two stationary points give a one-dimensional oscillatory integral with two nondegenerate critical points for 0<t<2pi. Uniform stationary phase applied to F_t/t controls t down to K/n. Diagonal Hessians Ut and Vt yield the logarithmic constant, while the difference-phase derivative stays bounded away from zero and makes the cross term O(1/n). Endpoint and interior estimates give the O(1/n) remainder. Positive a_j ensure both curvatures positive; q only shifts Fourier indices. A standalone independent arithmetic and autocorrelation quadrature checker is included; the infinite theorem rests on the explicit analytical estimates.

value.rationale: Critical ell-four summability is a natural threshold in the asymptotic spectral distribution of coefficients of inner-function powers, previously known only by its order for a single Blaschke factor. An exact curvature-dependent coefficient for any number of aligned zeros expresses how distinct zeros interact in a nontrivial asymptotic invariant. It permits quantitative comparison of different finite products and separates endpoint contributions, with an O(1/n) error rather than merely upper/lower growth bounds.
